segments: 466 [Book of the Chronography] they sent envoys to one another,
and summoned all the sons and relatives.
From the plains of the Steppes of Qipchaq [they summoned] Jochi, the eldest son,
and also Orda,
and Batu,
and Shiban,
and Tangqut,
and Berke,
and Berkecher,
and Boqa Timur,
and Aqnas,
and Chagatai.
And from the south they summoned Ögedei,
to whom the kingdom had been entrusted.
And from the east they summoned their uncle Otchigin,
and Bilgetei Noyan,
and Eljigidey Noyan,
and Tolui.
And the rest of the younger brothers were in the camp of Genghis Khan itself.
And they waited about two years, a little less, until their assembly was completed,
and they seated Ögedei upon the throne of the kingdom, as will be shown.
And in this same year died al-Malik al-Mu'azzam, son of al-Adil, the lord of Damascus and Jerusalem.
This man was formidable and dreadful,
and he had the ambition to reign over all regions.
And he appointed raiders who plundered the rest of the regions,
especially the territory of Hims and Hama.
And after him arose al-Malik al-Nasir Salah al-Din Dawud;
and both his uncles,
al-Malik al-Aziz and al-Malik al-Salih,
carried the saddlecloth before him.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and thirty-nine of the Greeks [1228 AD],
[AH] 625, al-Malik al-Kamil went forth from Egypt,
to come and take Damascus from his brother's son.
And when he came to Samaria,
the Emperor, the great king of the Germans (Armenians? {OCR}), went forth to Jaffa,
and al-Kamil was restrained from the affair of Damascus.
And his brother al-Ashraf came to him,
and al-Malik al-Mujahid, lord of Hims.
And they went and encamped upon Tell al-Ijjul,
and they sent envoys to the Emperor,
and learned the reason for his coming forth.
And the Emperor answered
that out of zeal for the house of the Lord he had come forth to Jerusalem.
And the Muslims surrendered Jerusalem to the Franks,
yet the city alone, apart from the territory;
and there was peace.
In this year Hassun, the physician of Edessa, died.
